system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: In MVFA's few-shot inference, the released code min-max normalises the zero-shot (text) branch and the few-shot (memory-bank) branch with the minimum and maximum over the entire test set and adds them with a fixed weight of 0.5, so the score of one image depends on the rest of the test set and a single incoming image cannot be scored. Can this transductive normalisation be replaced by an inductive one computed only from the K normal support images, at a small cost in AUROC? The inductive normaliser maps each branch's patch scores through the 1st and 99th percentiles of the leave-one-out patch scores of the supports (every patch of support i scored against the memory bank of the other K-1 supports and against the text anchors), which gives thousands of reference values even at K = 2; the fusion weight and the max pooling of the image score are kept fixed. Primary outcome: image-level and pixel-level AUROC of inductive versus transductive normalisation on each held-out BMAD dataset for K in {2, 4, 8, 16}. Motivating measurement: the spread of the original method's AUROC across random half-size test subsets and at shifted prevalence (10% and 50% abnormal). Secondary outcome: sensitivity at 95% specificity with a threshold fixed from the support scores alone.

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Leave-one-out empirical-CDF normalisation for inductive MVFA scoring
SUMMARY: Replace test-set min-max with each branch's (and level's) leave-one-out empirical CDF over support-normal patch scores; keep the 0.5 fusion and max pooling.
HYPOTHESIS: At K >= 4, LOO empirical-CDF normalisation keeps image and pixel AUROC within 1 point of the transductive pipeline, and its support-derived threshold gives realised specificity within 5 points of 95% on every held-out dataset, with a smaller miss than the percentile normaliser at K = 2.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: normaliser (test-set min-max; support percentiles as in the problem; support LOO empirical CDF). Reference set R_bl: patch scores of each support computed against a memory bank of the other K-1 supports (few-shot) or the text anchors (zero-shot). F_bl(s) = (rank of s in R_bl + 0.5)/(|R_bl| + 1); fused map = 0.5 F_zero + 0.5 F_few (averaged over levels as in MVFA); image score = max of fused map. Dependent variables: image/pixel AUROC; sensitivity at 95% specificity with tau = 95th percentile of LOO support image scores; realised specificity; per-image score shift under test-set resampling (exactly zero by construction for inductive variants).
RATIONALE: Percentiles use two points of the support distribution and are noisy for small K. Following ReCAP's non-parametric normal memory, each branch can instead be mapped through the full leave-one-out empirical CDF of support-normal patch scores, which places both branches on the same [0, 1] scale defined only by the K supports, before MVFA's unchanged 0.5 fusion and max pooling.
METHOD: 1) test_few.py: refactor into score_image(x, model, support_feats, refs) that uses no other test image; remove the test-set min-max block. 2) utils.py: build_refs(support_feats, text_feats): for i in 1..K, few-shot patch scores of support i against the bank of the others and zero-shot scores; store sorted arrays per branch and level. 3) cdf(s, R) via torch.searchsorted. 4) Fusion 0.5/0.5 and max pooling unchanged. Hyper-parameters: none beyond nominal specificity 95%; no training.
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA checkpoints retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std; fusion weight 0.5 and max pooling unchanged in every variant. Baselines: the original transductive pipeline (test-set min-max) and the percentile normaliser of the problem statement (1st/99th percentiles of leave-one-out support patch scores). Motivating measurement for all variants: AUROC spread of the transductive pipeline over random half-size test subsets and at 10% and 50% prevalence. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, realised specificity, ECE after a logistic map fitted on source validation. Falsified if AUROC drops by more than 1 point at K >= 4.

Idea B:
TITLE: Matched-support normalisation: normalise each test image against its most similar supports
SUMMARY: Instead of per-position statistics (which assume alignment) or a global analytic scale, normalise each test image's branch scores with the leave-one-out scores of the m supports whose global CLIP embedding is closest to it.
HYPOTHESIS: Normalising with the m = min(3, K) nearest supports improves pixel AUROC by at least 1 point over global support percentiles at K >= 8 on all six held-out datasets, including the unaligned ChestXray and HIS where position-wise normalisation does not apply.
RATIONALE: The position-wise parent captures that normal score levels vary with anatomy, but assumes images are aligned; the anchor-geometry parent shows that a branch's scale is set by global properties of the representation. A different mechanism follows: anatomy and acquisition vary per image, and the supports that look most like a test image carry the most relevant normal score distribution. Choosing the reference per test image by global embedding similarity handles variation without spatial alignment and stays inductive, since it uses only the supports.
METHOD: 1) utils.py: support_cls(supports): CLS embeddings of the supports (frozen CLIP). 2) test_few.py: for a test image, cosine similarity of its CLS to the supports; select top m; reference set = their LOO patch scores per branch and level; normalise with 1st/99th percentiles of that set; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. 3) Hyper-parameters: m in {1, 3, 5}. No training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baseline: position-wise normalisation. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity. Falsified if no gain over global percentiles at K >= 8.

Respond in exactly this format:
REASONING: <one to three sentences explaining your choice>
CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>
response:
REASONING: Idea A directly and cleanly addresses the specific mechanism of the transductive failure in MVFA by replacing test-set min-max with an empirical CDF over leave-one-out support patch scores, naturally calibrating both zero-shot and few-shot branches to a uniform [0, 1] scale without introducing arbitrary nearest-support filtering. In contrast, Idea B introduces an unjustified dynamic nearest-support selection heuristic ($m$ nearest supports) that severely restricts reference sample size at small $K$ and risks biasing the normalisation reference if the test image contains an anomaly that shifts its global embedding.
CONFIDENCE: HIGH
WINNER=A
